sorry_inventory.statement: theorem flo_succ (𝒮 : FloSeq 𝒯 Atom G₀) (σ : Stage) (hflo : FLO 𝒮 σ) : FLO 𝒮 (σ + 1) -- one sorry remaining, in the FLO-2 clause's `redundantEdge` case, sub-case `x = a, y = b` where the edge (a,b) is genuinely new (not inherited from stage σ)
sorry_inventory.assumption: Assumes the newly-adjoined redundant edge (a,b)'s introduction stage coheres with FLO-2's exact-locality requirement `max (rankOf a) (rankOf b) = sInf {τ | edge τ}`.
sorry_inventory.why_deferred: CONFIRMED (proved, not merely suspected) mathematically inadmissible for an unconstrained FloSeq: stepExt's `.redundantEdge a b` case has no side condition tying its introduction stage to `max (rankOf a, rankOf b)`. For a, b both already present at σ (so rankOf a, rankOf b ≤ σ via FloSeq.mono) and the edge genuinely new at σ+1, FLO-2 would force `max(rankOf a, rankOf b) = σ+1`, contradicting `max(rankOf a, rankOf b) ≤ σ < σ+1`. This resolves the plan's own Phase 2 task-list hedge ('confirm this is admissible under FLO-2 or that redundant-edge additions are handled by the maximality argument rather than the construction trace') in favor of the second branch: the maximality argument (raw_edge_of_tclosure) must force the edge present BEFORE the schedule invokes .redundantEdge, i.e. Phase 4's fair schedule needs a side condition ruling out premature/adversarial redundant-edge scheduling, or FloTask/FLO needs revision. All other flo_succ sub-cases (formula, diaWitness, skip, and the 'edge already present' half of redundantEdge) are sorry-free. UNAFFECTED by Phase 3 (flo_limit is a separate, unconditionally sorry-free theorem).
sorry_inventory.follow_up_task: Plan v5 Phase 4 (primeC'_exists_maximal): constrain the fair schedule so .redundantEdge is only exercised when raw_edge_of_tclosure has already forced the edge present (making this branch a no-op), or revise FloTask/FLO to encode that constraint explicitly, then close this sorry.
